title: The headless claude child of a runner has no turn or wall-clock bound, so a hung or looping run holds one of the two runner slots forever
goal: autopilot.py bounds each run of the headless child with a turn limit (--max-turns) and a wall-clock deadline (module constants, environment overrides for tests) that ends the child's process tree and records the cause timeout, and runner-status and status show a run's age and mark one past its deadline stalled; planted-failure tests cover the turn limit in the claude argv, the deadline ending a sleeping fake child, and the age line; found by the SP-4xngzagf review

run: import sys,pathlib;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import autopilot;argv=autopilot.claude_argv(pathlib.Path("."),"SP-aaaaaaaa");print(argv);sys.exit(0 if any(a.startswith("--max-turns") for a in argv) else 1)

gates.question: Which defaults bound a runner's headless child: the turn limit (--max-turns) and the wall-clock deadline (a loop guard above a run's turns before its first compaction, a deadline above a run with a full test suite; both replaceable by KB_RUNNER_MAX_TURNS and KB_RUNNER_DEADLINE_S)?
What does runner start exit with when the deadline ended the child (cause timeout)?
